Nice — fun trip ahead! Based on what you’ve been discussing about Strat vs Les Paul, open D tuning, and coil-splitting, here are practical things to look for when shopping for a new electric guitar:

- Decide the sounds you want first: what genres or songs you’ll play most. Les Pauls favor warm, thick, sustainful tones (great for rock, hard rock, heavier styles); Strat-style guitars tend to be brighter and more glassy.
- Body, weight, and feel: Les Pauls are often heavier (mahogany body with maple top) and have a set neck; Strats are contoured and usually lighter with a bolt-on neck. Pick what feels comfortable when you hold and play it.
- Neck profile and playability: try several neck shapes and frets to see which suits your hand and technique (comfort matters more than specs).
- Pickups and tonal options: check pickup type (humbucker vs single-coil) and whether the guitar has coil-tap/coil-splitting or other wiring options — coil-splitting gives more tonal flexibility if you want both big humbucker tones and brighter single-coil sounds.
- Setup and hardware: inspect action, intonation, and tuners. Playable setup matters a lot — low buzz, stable tuning, and comfortable action are key.
- Strings and tuning considerations: if you plan to use alternate tunings like open D or lower tunings, consider a heavier gauge string set and confirm the guitar feels and intonates well in those tunings.
- Try it through your amp and pedals: sound is the combo of guitar, amp, and pedals. Bring a cable and try your preferred amp or ask to test through the store’s amp with settings you like.
- Acoustic-style playing: if you want to do fingerpicking or acoustic-like parts (e.g., Blackbird-like parts), try the guitar unplugged and amplified — some Les Pauls can handle fingerpicked parts well, but body/strings/pickup choice affect the feel and tone.
- Weight the pros/cons: consider versatility (coil-splitting, pickup configuration), tone you prefer, and comfort. Ask about recent setup, warranty, and return policy.

Quick checklist to bring to the store: a short list of songs/tones you want, preference for pickups (humbucker vs single-coil), whether coil-splitting matters, preferred neck feel, and whether you’ll use alternate tunings or heavier strings. Play several guitars for at least 10–15 minutes each through an amp you like before deciding.

Have fun — if you want, tell me the styles you play and I can narrow recommendations further.
